bug_info.bug_desc: The old resolution-truncation logic in pwm_chan did not correctly clear the unused lower bits of phase_delay_i and duty_cycle_actual. It compared the input value against 16'h1 << (dc_resn_i + 1), then conditionally shifted right by lshift and unconditionally shifted left by lshift. For values below the comparison threshold this effectively multiplied the value by 2^lshift, while for values above the threshold the right-shift followed by left-shift restored the original value, leaving the low bits intact. As a result, with reduced dc_resn the computed on_phase/off_phase could be far too large or not truncated at all, producing incorrect PWM duty cycles.
bug_info.fix_hint: Replace the compare-and-shift scheme with direct clearing of the unused low bits. Compute a mask that keeps only the top dc_resn_i+1 bits, e.g. dc_mask = 16'hffff >> (dc_resn_i + 1), then assign phase_delay_masked = phase_delay_i & ~dc_mask and duty_cycle_masked = duty_cycle_actual & ~dc_mask. Use these masked values directly for on_phase and off_phase without additional scaling shifts.
